digest.lead: A federal judge has blocked the Pentagon's attempt to label Anthropic as a supply chain risk, delivering a major legal victory for the AI company amid escalating tensions with the Trump administration.
digest.summary: Meanwhile, Anthropic continues technical development with Claude Code v2.1.85 and leaked reports suggest testing of a more powerful 'Claude Mythos' model, while the company adjusts usage limits during peak hours.

stories.headline: Federal Judge Blocks Pentagon's Supply Chain Risk Designation for Anthropic
stories.summary: A federal judge granted a preliminary injunction blocking the Pentagon's effort to designate Anthropic as a supply chain risk [3][4]. The ruling came after heated courtroom exchanges, with Judge Rita Lin making pointed remarks about the case's stakes [8].
key_points: Court documents show the injunction was granted after Anthropic challenged the Pentagon designation
The case has drawn significant attention with nearly 200 comments on discussion forums
stories.impact: This legal victory protects Anthropic's ability to work with government contractors and could set precedent for how AI companies are regulated under national security frameworks.

stories.headline: Leaked Reports Suggest Anthropic Testing 'Claude Mythos' Model
stories.summary: A data leak has revealed that Anthropic is internally testing a new AI model called 'Claude Mythos' that reportedly represents a significant capability upgrade [2].
stories.impact: If confirmed, this suggests Anthropic is preparing its next-generation model release, which could reshape competitive dynamics in the AI market.

sources.title: A leak reveals that Anthropic is testing a more capable AI model "Claude Mythos"

stories.headline: Anthropic Adjusts Usage Limits During Peak Hours
stories.summary: Anthropic has implemented changes to discourage Claude usage during peak productivity hours, adjusting session limits to manage demand [5][7]. The company has also made updates to its subprocessor agreements [6].
stories.impact: These changes affect heavy Claude users who may need to adjust their workflows around new usage patterns, particularly during business hours.

sources.title: Anthropic discourages Claud demand during peak productivity hours

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.85 Adds MCP Server Management and Hook Filtering
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code release introduces environment variables for MCP server configuration, allowing one helper to serve multiple servers [1]. The update also adds conditional filtering for hooks using permission syntax and improves transcript logging for scheduled tasks [1].
key_points: New `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME` and `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL` variables simplify multi-server setups
Conditional hooks reduce overhead by filtering when processes run
Timestamp markers now appear when scheduled tasks like `/loop` and `CronCreate` execute
stories.impact: These improvements streamline MCP server management for developers running complex multi-server configurations and reduce system resource usage through smarter hook execution.

stories.headline: Open Source Project Claims $500 GPU Outperforms Claude Sonnet on Coding
stories.summary: A GitHub project called ATLAS claims that a $500 GPU setup can outperform Claude Sonnet on coding benchmarks [9]. The project has generated significant discussion in the developer community.
stories.impact: If validated, this could influence cost-conscious developers to consider local alternatives for coding tasks, though real-world performance may vary from benchmark results.

sources.title: $500 GPU outperforms Claude Sonnet on coding benchmarks

stories.headline: Use environment variables to configure MCP server settings in Claude Code
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.85 introduced CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME and CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variables for MCP headersHelper scripts. This allows a single helper script to serve multiple MCP servers, simplifying configuration management.
actionable_steps: Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME environment variable to your desired server name
Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variable to your MCP server URL
Update your MCP headersHelper scripts to use these variables instead of hardcoded values

stories.headline: Enable PowerShell tool for Windows development workflows
stories.summary: Claude Code now includes an opt-in PowerShell tool that allows Windows users to execute PowerShell commands directly through Claude. This provides native Windows command-line access for system administration and development tasks.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.84 or later
Enable the PowerShell tool in your settings as a preview feature

stories.headline: Write a CLAUDE.md file to set project conventions once
stories.summary: Adding a CLAUDE.md to your project root lets you define coding standards, test commands, and architectural decisions that persist across every Claude Code session. Think of it as onboarding documentation that Claude reads automatically — you teach it once instead of repeating yourself.
actionable_steps: Create a CLAUDE.md in your project root with build/test/lint commands
Add coding conventions like naming patterns, preferred libraries, and file structure
Include architectural decisions and constraints Claude should respect
Use /init in Claude Code to auto-generate a starter CLAUDE.md

stories.headline: Use managed settings drop-in directory for team policy deployment
stories.summary: The new managed-settings.d/ directory allows multiple teams to deploy independent configuration fragments that automatically merge. This enables better organization of team-specific policies without conflicts.
actionable_steps: Create a managed-settings.d/ directory alongside your managed-settings.json
Place individual team policy files in the directory (they merge alphabetically)
Name files with prefixes to control merge order (e.g., 01-team-a.json, 02-team-b.json)

stories.headline: Use Claude's extended thinking for complex architectural decisions
stories.summary: When asking Claude to make non-trivial design choices — like choosing between patterns, structuring a new module, or planning a migration — enabling extended thinking produces significantly better results. Claude will reason through trade-offs before committing to an approach, catching issues that quick responses miss.
actionable_steps: For architecture questions, ask Claude to 'think through the trade-offs' explicitly
Use Claude Code's plan mode (shift+tab) for multi-step tasks that need careful reasoning
Review Claude's reasoning in extended thinking to catch flawed assumptions early

sources.title: Tips for getting better architectural advice from Claude
